PRINCIPLE: Each test should focus on a single behavior. RATIONALE: Single Arrange-Act-Assert helps identify root cause. EVALUATION CRITERIA: A single Act (method call) and one assertion indicates atomicity. DECISION RULES: 1) Count Act operations (>1 => non-compliant). 2) Check name for multiple operations. 3) If one call + one assertion, compliant. PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on each other. RATIONALE: Enables parallel, order-independent execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Use of local variables and no shared mutable state favors independence. DECISION RULES: 1) If @Before/@After used, lean compliant. 2) If mutable static/instance vars modified without setup, non-compliant. 3) If only local variables used, compliant. VERDICT: The test uses only local variables and does not modify shared state in the method body, so compliant.

DECISION RULES: 1) If all tests only use valid inputs, non-compliant. 2) If assertThrows/@Test(expected) present, compliant. 3) If <2 test methods, likely only happy path -> non-compliant.
